codebase.title: FFTPACK 5.1 fast Fourier transforms
codebase.fingerprint_algorithm: SHA-256 over typed sorted regular-file paths+bytes and symlink paths+safe targets

agent_authored.description: FFTPACK 5.1 is a Fortran 77 library of normalized fast Fourier transforms by Paul Swarztrauber (NCAR, 2004-2011): complex and real transforms in 1D, 2D and for multiple sequences, plus sine, cosine and quarter-wave sine and cosine transforms, each as an initialize/forward/backward routine triplet with an error flag. It is vendored as its own codebase from the NCAR-Classic-Libraries-for-Geophysics container repository, which redistributes five unrelated libraries as tarballs.
evidence: README.md and OVERVIEW of the upstream container repository
doc/README_* and the HTML manual under doc/

build.system: make (GNU make; one top-level Makefile per library, each including a make.inc that selects the compiler by `uname -s`; src/ builds a static library, test/ compiles and immediately runs every test program)
commands: make MAKE=make AR=ar F90="gfortran -fdefault-real-8 -O2 -std=legacy -J LIBDIR -I LIBDIR" CPP="gfortran -cpp -E"   (double precision, the darwin.dp reference build)
make MAKE=make AR=ar F90="gfortran -O2 -std=legacy -J LIBDIR -I LIBDIR" CPP="gfortran -cpp -E"   (single precision, the darwin.sp reference build)
pitfalls: make.inc chooses the compiler from `uname -s`: on Linux it wants pgf90 or g95, on Darwin gfortran but MAKE := the hard-coded gmake path, which does not exist on current macOS; override MAKE=make AR=ar F90=... on the make command line (all five libraries)

gfortran 15.2 (and every gfortran >= 10) refuses the Fortran 77 argument-type and rank mismatches in FFTPACK, FISHPACK and SPHEREPACK ("Type mismatch between actual argument ... REAL(8) vs COMPLEX(8)", "Rank mismatch in argument theta") unless -std=legacy (or -fallow-argument-mismatch) is given; measured: fftpack 12 errors, spherepack 2 errors without it

the shipped darwin.dp transcripts were produced with -fdefault-real-8; the libraries are written for single precision and the darwin.sp build reproduces fewer digits (FISHPACK 1 to 4 digits, MUDPACK 0 to 2) and mudpack tcud3cr does not converge in single precision (ierror -10 here, ierror -4 and NaN in the shipped darwin.sp)
wall_s is the double-precision `make` run, which includes the 8 test runs the test Makefile executes (under 2 s in total); the single-precision build took the same

pitfalls.symptom: make: pgf90/g95 not found (Linux) or the hard-coded gmake path not found (macOS)
pitfalls.workaround: make MAKE=make AR=ar F90="gfortran -fdefault-real-8 -O2 -std=legacy -J LIBDIR -I LIBDIR" CPP="gfortran -cpp -E"

pitfalls.symptom: gfortran >= 10: Error: Type mismatch between actual argument ... (REAL(8) vs COMPLEX(8)); Error: Rank mismatch in argument theta
every run prints a different max error (5e-16 to 8e-16)
pitfalls.workaround: the tests call RANDOM_SEED() without arguments; a check must fix its input vector (or seed) itself and grade the round-trip error as an invariant

pitfalls.symptom: every test program writes only to stdout; the test Makefile pattern rule runs each executable right after linking it (the pattern rule executes the program it just linked), so `make` in test/ is build plus run and output/darwin.dp is the whole transcript
pitfalls.workaround: run the .exe files again by hand to capture per-test stdout

not_run.why: other platforms; compared against darwin.dp only

modules.title: FFTPACK 5.1 fast Fourier transforms
entrypoints: test/t*.f drivers calling the {C,R}FFT{1,2,M}{I,F,B}, COSQ, COST, SINQ and SINT triplets in src/
modules.expensive_path: the mixed-radix transform kernels (c1f*, r1f*, cmf*, mradf*, mradb*) under the multiple-transform routines cfftmf/rfftmf on long or many vectors
modules.rationale: The whole library is one module: one build (make, one static library), one test set, one scientific responsibility. FFTPACK 5.1 (Swarztrauber, NCAR, 2004-2011) computes normalized fast Fourier transforms of real and complex data, sine and cosine transforms and their quarter-wave forms, in 1D, 2D and for multiple sequences, each as an initialize/forward/backward triplet. It is vendored from the NCAR-Classic-Libraries-for-Geophysics container repository as its own codebase because the container holds five unrelated libraries that share no source; this one is packaged alone.
hazards: the eight test drivers draw their vectors from RANDOM_NUMBER after an unseeded RANDOM_SEED(), so a check has to fix its own input
written for single precision; the shipped references are the -fdefault-real-8 build
Fortran 77 argument-type aliasing needs -std=legacy under gfortran >= 10
modules.purpose: The whole library is one module: one build (make, one static library), one test set, one scientific responsibility. FFTPACK 5.1 (Swarztrauber, NCAR, 2004-2011) computes normalized fast Fourier transforms of real and complex data, sine and cosine transforms and their quarter-wave forms, in 1D, 2D and for multiple sequences, each as an initialize/forward/backward triplet. It is vendored from the NCAR-Classic-Libraries-for-Geophysics container repository as its own codebase because the container holds five unrelated libraries that share no source; this one is packaged alone.
primary_inputs: a real or complex data array of length N (or L x M for 2D, or LOT sequences with stride) and its work/save arrays initialised by the I routine of the triplet
primary_outputs: the transformed array in place, normalized so that forward then backward reproduces the input; an integer error flag IER
algorithm_stages: factorisation of N into radices 2, 3, 4, 5 and general (factor, mcfti1/rffti1)
mixed-radix butterfly passes (c1f*, r1f*, cmf*, mradf*, mradb*)
real-to-complex and complex-to-real packing (r2w, w2r) and the sine/cosine pre- and post-processing
unique_responsibilities: all discrete Fourier, sine, cosine and quarter-wave transforms of the package
not_responsible_for: no PDE solving; the elliptic solvers in FISHPACK, MUDPACK and SPHEREPACK carry their own older FFT copies
evidence: src/ (the library), test/ (the drivers), Makefile and make.inc
runs.json: every driver built and run natively
modules.classification: agent-authored module card; CLI-computed size and approval status
